source.title: Generalization Through The Lens Of Leave-One-Out Error
source.authors: Gregor Bachmann; Thomas Hofmann; Aurélien Lucchi

record.tranche_reason: Uses leave-one-out estimates with NTK and random-feature kernel models to test whether they track test generalization under label noise and model-width changes; this is a conceptual test of V1 and V2.
record.gate_note: The study reports own results for test and LOO errors/accuracies under randomized labels and across model width, plus depth and transfer-learning comparisons. It does not test the other mapped claim versions. Cited findings from Zhang et al. (2017) are background, not rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own held-out results under label randomization and width changes in NTK and random-feature models, bearing on V1 and V2 through a different training method. Agreement between LOO and test performance alone does not establish either version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that closed-form LOO loss and accuracy capture generalization behavior in kernel-regime models, including label noise and double descent, and predict top-layer transfer-learning performance. They also prove a LOO-loss spike under their stated spectral assumption.
record.recipe_differences: Kernel-regime NTK and random-feature models with leave-one-out estimates; not the finite networks and standard gradient-training recipes in the mapped originals. Code for numerical experiments is released.
record.method_sensitivity: Label noise level and model width change the measured generalization behavior; depth also changes correspondence between LOO and test quantities, with a small loss gap for very shallow models and a reported 0.015 loss gap for MNIST.

fits_no_version.finding: Test and LOO squared losses spike near interpolation even though random-label classification accuracy remains at chance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interpolation can produce a squared-loss peak without a corresponding classification-accuracy peak.

fits_no_version.finding: LOO loss and accuracy closely track their test counterparts across label-noise and width settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Closed-form LOO estimates predict held-out performance in the tested kernel regimes.

record.problems: Key curves are figure-only without numerical values in the supplied text. The random-label and width experiments use kernel or random-feature models, so they do not directly reproduce the finite-network recipes in V1 or V2. Double-descent theory assumes a Haar-distributed kernel rotation matrix.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. Figures 1, 2, 3, 6, and 7 provide several additional figure-only comparisons; only the results bearing on V1 or V2 are recorded. Transfer-learning table results do not test a mapped version.

untested.parts: The original finite-network architectures and training recipes are not evaluated. The binary random-feature experiment lacks a matched natural-label comparison; the NTK experiment's numerical accuracy endpoints cannot be recovered from the supplied figure-free text.

End-to-end training of one-hidden-layer ReLU networks with standard gradient methods and the downsampled CIFAR-10 setting are not evaluated; the width experiment fits only the output layer on binary MNIST.
No controlled convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurements or ranking of generalization gaps.
No removal of highly memorized examples compared with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains figure captions but no readable curves. Exact accuracy values cannot be verified. Differences in architecture or training method are scope differences, not evidence that a version fails. The paper is not an original source for these versions.

versions.untested_parts: Tests randomized-label behavior in kernel and random-feature models, not the same finite Inception, AlexNet, and MLP architectures and recipes described in the version.
Tests a binary MNIST random-feature model as width varies, not one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on both MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10.

rows.subject: 5-layer fully-connected NTK model
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST with increasingly randomized labels; measured test and leave-one-out loss and accuracy against clean targets.

conditions.value: increasingly perturbing the targets with noise

rows.measure: Test and LOO loss and accuracy as a function of label noise
rows.note: Authors state there is an almost perfect match between test and LOO quantities across all settings; plotted numerical values are not given in text.
rows.check: Test accuracy under label noise is relevant, but the supplied text omits the plotted accuracy values and endpoints. Almost perfect LOO–test agreement does not establish above-chance natural-label accuracy and chance-level random-label accuracy. Zero training loss follows from the full-rank, unregularized kernel setting rather than a reported training measurement.

rows.subject: 5-layer fully-connected NTK model
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR10 with increasingly randomized labels; measured test and leave-one-out loss and accuracy against clean targets.

conditions.value: increasingly perturbing the targets with noise

rows.measure: Test and LOO loss and accuracy as a function of label noise
rows.note: Authors state there is an almost perfect match between test and LOO quantities across all settings; plotted numerical values are not given in text.
rows.check: The supplied text reports LOO–test agreement without readable test-accuracy endpoints. This cannot establish the full V1 comparison. Separate test accuracy from loss and estimator agreement; record kernel interpolation as an analytical property.

rows.subject: random feature model
rows.operation_detail: Fit to binary MNIST with fully randomized labels while width varied; measured test accuracy and loss.
rows.note: Text states the model is randomly guessing throughout all overparameterization regimes; no numerical accuracy is given.
rows.check: The authors explicitly report chance-level test accuracy at every width, including interpolating widths. This establishes the random-label component only; this experiment supplies no matched natural-label comparison.

rows.subject: random feature model
rows.operation_detail: Fit to binary MNIST with fully randomized labels while width varied; measured test and LOO loss.
rows.note: Text states both test and LOO loss exhibit a strong spike around the interpolation threshold; plotted numerical values are not given.
rows.check: A squared-loss spike under random labels does not measure V1's accuracy comparison or V2's continued improvement in classification test error.

rows.subject: random feature model
rows.operation_detail: Varied feature width and measured training, test, and LOO loss and accuracy.
rows.measure: Test loss and accuracy across width
rows.note: Figure caption identifies the measures, and text says test error spikes at the interpolation threshold and then decreases as complexity grows; values are only plotted.
rows.check: The reversed state and challenges verdict misinterpret double descent. The reported decrease beyond interpolation agrees with V2; the spike at interpolation does not contradict improvement beyond it. Separate classification accuracy from squared loss, and specify that only the output layer is fitted.

rows.subject: random feature model
rows.operation_detail: Varied feature width and measured training, test, and LOO loss and accuracy.
rows.measure: LOO loss and accuracy across width
rows.note: Authors state LOO closely follows test error, exhibiting the spike at interpolation; subsequent decrease in error is visible only in the figure.
rows.check: This row measures an estimator's agreement with test performance, rather than held-out performance itself. It is auxiliary evidence for the LOO method, not an independent test of V2.

relationships.condition: Random-label component: binary MNIST random-feature models, including interpolating widths
relationships.reason: R3 explicitly reports chance-level test accuracy throughout the width sweep, consistent with V1's random-label prediction; it does not establish the matched natural-label component.
relationships.display_finding: Test accuracy stayed at chance throughout the width sweep, including interpolating widths, without establishing matched natural-label generalization.

relationships.condition: Natural-label binary MNIST with 5,000 samples and a varying-width random-feature model
relationships.reason: R5 reports double descent with declining test error beyond interpolation; the interpolation peak is not a reversal of V2's post-interpolation prediction.
relationships.display_finding: Test error declined on the wider branch beyond the interpolation peak.

relation.reason: The study reports its own test accuracy and loss under randomized labels and varying width, directly bearing on V1's random-label component and V2.

tranche.reason: Kernel-regime NTK and random-feature experiments measure held-out performance under label randomization and width changes using a different method from the claim's original finite-network training.

source_check.notes: Both rows correctly retain figure-only values without inventing numerical performance. The authors' conclusion paraphrase is accurate; LOO agreement alone does not establish the mapped claims.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: 5-layer fully-connected NTK models on MNIST and CIFAR10 with label noise varied
reader_labels.reason: Test and LOO loss and accuracy closely match across the noise settings, including randomized labels (R1–R2). The random-label test accuracy is not reported as a separate natural-label comparison.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: random-feature model on binary MNIST with fully randomized labels across widths
reader_labels.reason: The test accuracy remains random guessing, and the test and LOO losses spike near interpolation (R3–R4); this is not a finite neural-network natural-label training comparison.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: random-feature model on binary labeled MNIST across width
reader_labels.reason: Test error spikes around interpolation, then falls as width increases further, so the claim of continued monotonic lowering beyond zero training error does not hold across the full sweep (R5–R6).
